title: New External Device Recognition Audit
exclusions: Reports Windows Security Event ID 6416, which Microsoft defines as a new external device recognized by the system. It is not limited to USB or storage: printers, redirected devices, biometrics, docks, and other Plug and Play classes can appear. The derived `usb_storage_or_portable` label requires a `USB\` device-instance prefix plus `DiskDrive` or `WPD` class, but it does not prove removable media, mount, file access, copy, execution, exfiltration, policy violation, or malicious hardware. Event 6416 commonly records the computer account/SYSTEM rather than the person who inserted a device. Device enable/disable/policy events 6419-6424 and file/DLP/Defender Device Control evidence are separate. The local index is a deployment choice; no compliance or prevention assurance is claimed.
evidence: Retain `windows_new_external_device_6416` definition, ACL, schedule and results; effective Audit PNP Activity policy; source-health coverage; every raw 6416 XML record with endpoint, subject, DeviceId, DeviceDescription, ClassId, ClassName, VendorIds, CompatibleIds, LocationInformation, EventRecordID and time; Device Manager or endpoint-management comparison; approved-device inventory revision; dated controls; analyst disposition; alert delivery; and bounded exceptions. This documentation-only review connected no device and generated no event, search, alert, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index, ingest Security Event ID 6416 with `Computer=SERVER01`, `SubjectUserName=SERVER01$`, `DeviceId=USB\\VID_1234&PID_5678\\ABC001`, `DeviceDescription=Approved Lab USB Disk`, `ClassId={4D36E967-E325-11CE-BFC1-08002BE10318}`, `ClassName=DiskDrive`, `VendorIds=USBSTOR...`, `CompatibleIds=USBSTOR\\Disk`, `LocationInformation=Port_#0001.Hub_#0002`, and `EventRecordID=6416001`. Expect one row with `device_scope=usb_storage_or_portable`, preserving the machine subject without relabeling it as the human user.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for Event ID 6419, 6416 from the System channel, and 6416 with empty endpoint or DeviceId. Separately, ingest a valid 6416 with `DeviceId=SWD\\PRINTENUM...` and `ClassName=PrintQueue`; expect one row classified `external_other`, not USB storage and not suppressed.

dataSources: Windows Security XML Event ID 6416 under **Detailed Tracking > Audit PNP Activity**, collected with Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) into deployment-local `index=wineventlog`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`. Required Microsoft fields are `SubjectUserSid`, `SubjectUserName`, `SubjectDomainName`, `SubjectLogonId`, `DeviceId`, `DeviceDescription`, `ClassId`, `ClassName`, `VendorIds`, `CompatibleIds`, and `LocationInformation`, plus `Computer`, `EventRecordID`, and event ID. DeviceId is the device instance path; compare it and class properties in Device Manager.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742), version 10.0.1. Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Device Control or another DLP/device-control product is optional for enforcement and file-operation evidence.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:Security" EventCode=6416 earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval event_code=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID)), endpoint=lower(trim(coalesce(Computer,host))), device_id=trim(DeviceId), device_description=trim(DeviceDescription), class_name=trim(ClassName), class_id=trim(ClassId), subject_user=trim(SubjectUserName), normalized_device_id=lower(device_id), normalized_class=lower(class_name)
| where event_code=6416 AND len(endpoint)>0 AND len(device_id)>0
| eval device_scope=case(match(normalized_device_id,"^usb\\\\") AND in(normalized_class,"diskdrive","wpd"),"usb_storage_or_portable",match(normalized_device_id,"^usb\\\\"),"usb_other",true(),"external_other"), use_case="UC-1.2.91"
| table _time endpoint device_scope device_id device_description class_name class_id VendorIds CompatibleIds LocationInformation SubjectUserSid SubjectDomainName subject_user SubjectLogonId EventRecordID source sourcetype use_case
| sort 0 -_time endpoint device_id
description: Reports one row for each Security 6416 external-device recognition event and classifies it as USB storage/portable, other USB, or other external based only on the observed device instance path and class. The output preserves hardware metadata and the machine/security subject; it does not claim a human inserted media or moved files.
value: A centralized external-device trail helps asset, security, and support teams explain new hardware, verify sensitive-server policy, and pivot into device-control or file evidence when portable media is involved. Keeping all 6416 classes visible prevents a brittle USB-only filter from silently discarding redirected printers, docks, and other legitimate sources of audit noise.
implementation: Enable Success auditing for Audit PNP Activity on governed Windows systems, collect Security as XML, and validate 6416 fields against Device Manager. Save the SPL as `windows_new_external_device_6416`, schedule every five minutes over a closed delayed bucket, retain all classes, and notify only according to asset policy—for example any USB storage-class row on a server. Use separate device-control/DLP and object-access telemetry to prove blocking or file movement.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — External Device Audit`: Security-source and policy coverage first; new devices by scope/class; first-seen device IDs; sensitive-server USB rows; and a detail table with endpoint, description, device/class IDs, vendor/compatible IDs, location, subject, and EventRecordID. Drill down to raw XML, Device Manager/endpoint inventory, 6419-6424 policy events, device-control verdicts, logons, and file activity. Never label all 6416 events as removable storage.
dataModelAcceleration: No Change CIM substitute is claimed. Generic change rows do not preserve the device instance path, PnP class GUID/name, vendor/compatible IDs, location, or the exact 6416 semantics.

knownFalsePositives:
The event is true device recognition; policy determines whether it is concerning.

1. **USB keyboard, mouse, smart-card reader, biometric sensor, dock, or adapter** — Verify DeviceId, ClassName/ClassId, VendorIds, endpoint inventory, and approved hardware model. Route `usb_other` to inventory unless policy says otherwise; do not suppress all USB.

2. **Remote Desktop redirected printer or software print queue** — Microsoft examples show `SWD\PRINTENUM` and `PrintQueue` in 6416. Confirm active remote session, print-queue identity, class, and user/session evidence. Use `windows_external_device_exceptions.csv` only for an exact governed queue/device class and endpoint role.

3. **Approved encrypted removable drive used for backup, transfer, or incident response** — Match serial-bearing DeviceId, asset register, custodian, ticket, endpoint, purpose, and UTC window. Preserve the event; suppress duplicate notification only while the approved task is active.

4. **OS deployment, driver installation, firmware update, or hardware refresh** — Correlate deployment job, setup/driver events, technician, expected device list, and change window. Unknown devices or events after expiry remain visible.

5. **VDI/USB redirection or docking-station reconnect** — Verify broker/session, virtual endpoint, redirection policy, physical client, device identity, and repeat pattern. Scope exceptions to the exact pool/device and measured session window.

The post-result lookup requires endpoint, exact DeviceId or controlled class plus vendor/model, owner, reason, ticket, numeric start, and exclusive expiry. Never suppress by `ClassName=DiskDrive`, all servers, or machine-account subject.
reviewer: documentation-only Cursor AI editorial review against Microsoft Event 6416 and Audit PNP Activity, MITRE ATT&CK, and Splunk Windows add-on configuration; policy, device generation, class/provider fields, SPL, controls, source health, device inventory, notification, and file-movement correlation were specified but not executed or Microsoft/Splunk/endpoint-SME signed

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact device contract

Assign endpoint engineering, asset inventory, security/DLP, Splunk collection, and incident owners. Define policies by asset role: a new storage device on a domain controller differs from one on a managed workstation. Install Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows 10.0.1 on required tiers and restrict hardware/user context. Remove the prior unsupported compliance mappings; 6416 collection alone does not satisfy application control or ordered-operations obligations.

Microsoft defines 6416 as **a new external device was recognized by the system**. DeviceId is the device instance path, DeviceDescription the friendly description, ClassId the class GUID, and ClassName the device class. Subject often represents SYSTEM/the computer account. Do not call it the inserting person.

## Step 1 — Enable auditing and collect Security XML

Through Advanced Audit Policy set **Detailed Tracking > Audit PNP Activity** to Success for governed systems. Verify effective policy using `auditpol /get /subcategory:"Plug and Play Events"` or the localized supported equivalent plus winning GPO. Measure event volume on VDI and peripheral-heavy roles.

Collect `[WinEventLog://Security]` with `renderXml=true` in an app-owned `inputs.conf`, writing to deployment-local `index=wineventlog`. Verify effective stanza with `splunk btool inputs list WinEventLog://Security --debug`. In the Event Viewer console at **Windows Logs > Security**, compare fixed 6416 EventRecordIDs and all Data fields to Splunk XML extraction. Operate Security source-health per expected host.

## Step 2 — Save and understand the report

Save the sidecar SPL as `windows_new_external_device_6416`, schedule every five minutes over `earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m`, and retain all rows. It fixes the Security XML source and exact event ID, requires endpoint/device identity, then uses only observed DeviceId/ClassName to produce three triage scopes. `USB\` plus DiskDrive or WPD is a review priority, not proof of removable media. USB devices with other classes and non-USB external devices remain visible.

Configure the Universal Forwarder input and a least-privilege search-head RBAC role for this saved search. Keep its source restriction literal: `index=wineventlog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, and `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`; dispatch one closed event-time window lasting 5 minutes each run.

Apply alert policy after the base report: page on storage-class USB for sensitive servers, ticket first-seen devices on controlled workstations, and inventory other classes. Do not use a Change tstats count as a substitute.

## Step 3 — Validate device classes and identity

Run exact controls with fixed bounds. Test USB DiskDrive, other USB, SWD PrintQueue, empty fields, wrong channel/ID, case handling, and duplicate records. On a lab system connect only approved devices. In **Device Manager > device Properties > Details**, compare Device instance path, Device description, Class and Class GUID to the event. Record endpoint, physical device/serial-bearing identity, Windows/add-on/Splunk versions, expected/actual row, and operator.

Test 6419-6424 separately if device enable/disable or policy enforcement matters. Correlate Defender Device Control/DLP verdicts and file auditing in separate searches. Prove alert delivery, dashboard ACL, source health, lookup expiry, and a server-versus-workstation routing policy.

## Step 4 — Operationalize review and response

On a sensitive-server row: verify raw XML and source health; identify class, device path, vendor/compatible IDs, location, and endpoint role; check active logon/session and physical/change ownership; compare approved inventory; query device-control verdict and file activity when available; contact system/security owner; and preserve evidence.

Do not automatically disable the device, eject storage, delete files, lock the machine account, or attribute activity to `SubjectUserName`. A keyboard, dock, redirected printer, or emergency response drive can be operationally critical. Use approved endpoint controls for blocking.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **No 6416:** verify effective Audit PNP Activity, Security input, supported Windows version, channel retention, and source freshness.
- **Everything appears as SYSTEM/computer account:** expected for many PnP operations; correlate interactive/RDP logons and endpoint telemetry, do not rewrite the subject.
- **Printers look external:** 6416 covers external devices broadly; classify by SWD/PRINTENUM and PrintQueue rather than dropping the record.
- **Storage device class differs:** inspect actual Device Manager and XML fields on that hardware; update classification only with fixtures and source evidence.
- **Same device repeats:** compare full DeviceId, endpoint, EventRecordID, reconnect/reinstall behavior, and collection duplication.
- **WEF host is collector:** repair original Computer preservation before applying sensitive-server policy.
- **No file-copy evidence:** expected; 6416 is recognition, not mount or I/O. Add device-control/DLP/object-access telemetry rather than inferring transfer.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a record when Windows notices a new outside device, such as a drive, dock, printer, or keyboard. The details help the team check sensitive computers and investigate portable storage without pretending every plugged-in device moved data.
hardware: Windows endpoints and servers that support Audit PNP Activity. USB/device-control enforcement and file-operation visibility require additional endpoint or DLP tooling.
